title: N-Queens
statement: Place n queens on an n x n board so that no two attack each other (same row, column or diagonal). Return every distinct solution as a list of n strings made of 'Q' and '.'.

hints.1_question: Place one queen per row. For each row, which columns are still safe?
hints.2_nudge: Track occupied columns and both diagonal directions (row - col and row + col). Recurse row by row, undoing the placement afterwards.
hints.3_big_hint: bt(r): for c in range(n): skip if c in cols or r-c in d1 or r+c in d2; place; bt(r+1); remove. At r == n build the board strings.

known_bugs.name: ignores diagonals
known_bugs.followup: Two queens on the same diagonal attack each other. Where do you check diagonals?

known_bugs.name: checks only one diagonal direction
known_bugs.followup: A queen attacks along two diagonals: down-right and down-left. Which one do you track?

known_bugs.name: returns only the first solution
known_bugs.followup: The task asks for every solution. How many does n = 4 have?

followups: Why do row - col and row + col identify diagonals?
How would bitmasks speed this up?
